bibl.title: Electric Field Effect in Atomically Thin Carbon Films

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Here we report the electric field effect in a naturally occurring two-dimensional (2D) meterial that we refer to as few-layer graphene (FLG).

span.label: ambipolar electric field effect in few-layer graphene
span.quote: The films are found to be a twodimensional semimetal with a tiny overlap between valence and conductance bands and to exhibit a strong ambipolar electric-field effect such that electrons and holes in concentrations up to 1013cm-2 and with roomtemperature mobilities ≈10,000 cm2/Vs can be induced by applying gate voltage.

span.label: laboratory-experiment
span.quote: The reported graphene films were made by mechanical exfoliation (repeated peeling) of small mesas of highly-oriented pyrolytic graphite as described in the supporting online material [15].

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: atomically-thin (few-layer) graphene is stable and metallic under ambient conditions, and its carrier density is tunable by an electric field (ambipolar field effect), enabling ballistic transport
span.quote: monocrystalline graphitic films, which are just a few atoms thick but nonetheless stable under ambient conditions, metallic and of remarkably high quality

span.label: an observed shift could be due to unintentional doping by absorbed gas molecules
span.note: what this limits: the observed gate-voltage shift: THIS SHIFT COULD BE DUE TO AN UNINTENTIONAL DOPING OF THE FILMS BY ABSORBED GAS MOLECULES
span.quote: this shift could be due to an unintentional doping of the films by absorbed gas molecules

span.label: The zero-gate-voltage hole doping may be an artefact of adsorbed gas molecules rather than intrinsic.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - the zero-gate-voltage hole doping may be adsorbate, not intrinsic
span.quote: However, this shift could be due to an unintentional doping of the films by absorbed gas molecules [16,17].

span.label: The authors cannot explain why the measured behaviour fits a simple free-electron model when graphene is expected to have linear dispersion and massless carriers.
span.note: what this limits: the free-electron description of the transport data: GRAPHENE IS EXPECTED TO HAVE THE LINEAR ENERGY DISPERSION AND CARRIERS WITH ZERO MASS, AND THE REASON WHY THE OBSERVED BEHAVIOR IS SO WELL DESCRIBED BY THE SIMPLEST FREE-ELE[ctron model is unclear] - the fit is unexplained, not the failure
span.quote: Note that graphene is expected to have the linear energy 2 dispersion and carriers with zero mass, and the reason why the observed behavior is so well described by the simplest free-electron model remains to be understood.

span.label: The transistor's on-off resistance ratio is modest and this is a fundamental limit for a gapless material.
span.note: what this limits: the device application claim: GRAPHENE TRANSISTORS SHOW A RATHER MODEST ON-OFF RESISTANCE RATIO ... BUT THIS IS A FUNDAMENTAL LIMITATION FOR ANY MAT[erial without a gap]
span.quote: Graphene transistors show a rather modest on-off resistance ratio (less than ≈30 at 300K; limited because of thermally excited carriers) but this is a fundamental limitation for any material without a band gap exceeding kBT.

span.label: The devices differ in the one variable that defines the material - the number of layers - and that number is inferred from the measurement rather than known.
span.note: what this limits: the band overlap reported here as a property of the material: it varied from 4 to 20 meV across samples, which the authors attribute to a different number of graphene layers involved, inferred rather than independently established
span.quote: which varied from 4 to 20meV for different samples, presumably indicating a different number of graphene layers involved

span.label: The headline mobility is the top of a sample-to-sample range, and mobility is stated to be limited by defect scattering rather than intrinsic.
span.note: what this limits: the mobility figure quoted from this paper: measured values varied from sample to sample between 3,000 and 10,000, and were practically independent of temperature, which the authors read as still being limited by scattering on defects
span.quote: In both cases, we obtained the same values of µ, which varied from sample to sample between 3,000 and 10,000 cm2/V⋅s. The mobilities were practically independent of temperature T, indicating that even being so high they were still limited by scattering on defects

span.label: What is measured is few-layer graphene of one, two or three atomic layers reported together, not single-layer graphene.
span.note: what this limits: these results as measurements of single-layer graphene: the reported devices contained just 1, 2 or 3 atomic layers and all of them are reported as exhibiting essentially identical electronic properties
span.quote: electronic properties of our thinnest (FLG) devices, which contained just 1, 2 or 3 atomic layers [15]. All FLG devices exhibited essentially identical electronic properties

span.label: graphene - A NAME IN USE BEFORE ITS REFERENT EXISTED: a hypothetical single layer, employed to describe the properties of graphite, fullerenes and nanotubes, while planar graphene itself was presumed not to exist in the free state
span.quote: This hypothetical material is widely used to describe properties of many carbon-based materials, including graphite, large fullerenes, nanotubes, etc. (e.g., carbon nanotubes are usually thought of as graphene sheets rolled up into nm-sized cylinders) [5-7]. Planar graphene itself has so far been presumed not to exist in the free state, being rather unstable with respect to the formation of curved structures such as soot, fullerenes and nanotubes

span.label: graphene - AS MEASURED IN THIS PAPER: few-layer graphene, devices of one, two or three atomic layers pooled together, which is not the sense the word now carries
span.quote: electronic properties of our thinnest (FLG) devices, which contained just 1, 2 or 3 atomic layers

span.label: carrier mobility - MEASURED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS AND AGREEING: from the field effect and from magnetoresistance, which is the rarer and stronger case of two operationalisations converging
span.quote: Carrier mobilities in FLG were determined from field-effect and magnetoresistance measurements as µ = σ(Vg)/en(Vg) and µ = RH/ρ, respectively. In both cases, we obtained the same values

span.label: contradicts → the prior consensus (refs 5-14) that planar graphene cannot exist in the free state
span.quote: Contrary to the common belief, we have been able to prepare graphitic sheets of thicknesses down to a few atomic layers, including single layer graphene, and succeeded in making devices from them and studying their electronic properties.
